report:
Antecedentes Clínicos:
Gonalgia bilateral.
Hallazgos:
Transformación quística parcial del LCA. LCP y ligamentos colaterales dentro de límites normales.
Rotura que impresiona periférica del cuerno posterior y raíz meniscal posterior del menisco medial
con leve extrusión meniscal.
Extensa rotura compleja del cuerno anterior, cuerpo, cuerno posterior y parte de la raíz meniscal
posterior del menisco lateral con importante extrusión meniscal.
Úlceras condrales de espesor total con cambios óseos secundarios y proliferaciones óseas
periféricas del compartimento femorotibial lateral. Úlceras condrales de espesor parcial de la zona
de carga del compartimento femorotibial medial.
Úlceras condrales espesor total con cambios óseos secundarios la faceta lateral y vértice de la
rótula.
Condropatía superficial de la tróclea femoral.
Leve derrame articular. No hay quistes poplíteos patológicos. Formación quística polilobulada en
relación a la articulación tibio peronea proximal hacia anterior y posterior, sin signos de
complicación.
Leve engrosamiento y aumento de señal de la inserción distal del tendón cuadricipital y de la
inserción proximal del tendón rotuliano, sin signos de rotura.
Tendones de la pata de ganso, bíceps femoral y banda iliotibial dentro de límites normales.
Impresión:
Rotura periférica del menisco medial con leve extrusión.
Extensa rotura degenerativa del menisco lateral con extrusión.
Avanzados cambios degenerativos del compartimento femorotibial lateral.
Condropatía con lesiones grado 2 del compartimento femorotibial medial.
Condropatía con lesiones grado 4 de la rótula y superficie de la tróclea femoral.
Leve derrame articular.
Formaciones quísticas profundas en relación a la articulación tibio peronea proximal, no
complicadas.
Tendinosis rotuliana proximal y cuadricipital distal.

Antecedentes Clínicos:
Obs. Lesión meniscal medial.
Hallazgos:
No hay alteraciones de señal significativas de la médula ósea.
Aumento de señal difuso del LCA, sin signos que sugieran rotura categórica. LCP y ligamentos
colaterales dentro de límites normales.
Meniscos de morfología y señal conservada, sin criterios categóricos de rotura.
Condropatía superficial de la región central de la zona de carga del cóndilo femoral medial. El
resto de los cartílagos femorotibiales y patelofemoral sin alteraciones.
No hay significativo derrame articular ni quistes poplíteos.
Leve aumento de señal del tercio proximal del tendón rotuliano, sin signos de rotura. Tendón
cuadricipital, tendones de la pata de ganso, bíceps femoral y banda iliotibial dentro de límites
normales.
No hay alteraciones de señal significativas de la grasa de Hoffa.
Impresión:
Condropatía superficial de la región central de la zona de carga del cóndilo femoral medial.
Leve tendinosis rotuliana proximal

LEFT KNEE MRI 

CLINICAL INDICATION: Medial meniscus injury, query MCL tear

Technique: Multiplanar PD, PF fat sat and T1 imaging was acquired through the knee. 

Comparison: The x-ray [Date]

Findings:

General:
Marrow:  There is edema of the medial femoral condyle at the site of the MCL insertion, and in the posterolateral femoral condyle. There is edema in the medial proximal tibia and the posterolateral proximal tibia.
Consistent with internal bone contusion secondary valgus injury.
Effusion:  No significant effusion

Menisci:   
Medial meniscus:   Intact.
Lateral meniscus:   Intact.

Ligaments and tendons:
Cruciate ligaments:   There is increased signal in the PCL, which may be keeping with a low-grade tear. No tibial translation.
Medial collateral ligament:   High-grade partial-thickness tear of the proximal of the mid fibers of the superficial medial collateral ligament. Low-grade partial-thickness tear of the meniscal femoral as well as posterior plate components of the deep medial collateral ligament.
Lateral collateral ligament:   normal
Popliteofibular ligament:   normal
Other posterolateral corner ligaments:   normal
Popliteal tendon:   normal
Iliotibial band:   normal

Extensor mechanism:
Quadriceps tendon: Mild increased signal along the patellar insertion, in keeping with tendinosis
Patella:   normal
Patellar tendon:   normal
Hoffa?s fat pad: Subtle edema in keeping with impingement

Cartilage:
Patellofemoral joint: Mild chondrosis mainly along the trochlear aspect there
Medial compartment:   normal cartilage
Lateral compartment:  Mild chondrosis.

CONCLUSION:

1. Intact menisci.
2. High-grade partial thickness tear of the medial collateral ligament and bone contusions posterior lateral femoral condyle and lateral tibial plateau in keeping with valgus injury.
3. Mild chondrosis.
4. Mild quadriceps tendinosis without tear.

Findings:  No significant knee effusion. A moderate fluid-filled Baker's cyst is demonstrated.  Osteophyte formation is noted in all three compartments.  
There is moderate thinning and fraying of the medial compartment articular cartilage with degenerate tearing of the body of medial meniscus. A few loose intra-articular bodies are noted within the posterior joint recess and within the Baker's cyst.  The lateral compartment articular cartilage is preserved. Normal lateral meniscus.  
Normal ACL, PCL, MCL and LCL. Normal extensor mechanism.  Moderate - severe thinning and loss of the trochlear articular cartilage is noted with mild underlying bony change. The patellar articular cartilage is preserved.  
Conclusion: Moderate - severe medial compartment degeneration with degenerate tearing of the medial meniscus. Moderate - severe trochlear articular cartilage degeneration. Moderately large fluid-filled Baker's cyst.

Findings:  Minor thickening of the proximal MCL with no surrounding edema suggestive of previous injury and healing with scarring. Intact lateral collateral ligament and cruciate ligaments. Small 10 mm x 12 mm x 9 mm loculated ganglion cyst adjacent to the tibial attachment of the PCL.  On a background of severe mucoid degeneration the body and posterior horn of the lateral meniscus is severely attenuated in keeping with complex degenerate tearing, with a few small parameniscal cysts along the lateral joint line. Intact medial meniscus.  Normal appearance of the pes anserine tendons, popliteus tendon, distal biceps femoris tendon and distal iliotibial band.  Prominent enthesopathy at the superior pole of the patella at the quadriceps tendon incision. Normal patella tendon.  Low-grade chondral thinning in the lateral tibiofemoral compartment. Focal 2 mm x 2 mm low-grade cartilage defect in the weightbearing portion of the medial femoral condyle. Otherwise well maintained medial tibiofemoral hyaline articular cartilage. Relatively well-maintained patellofemoral hyaline articular cartilage.  
Conclusion:  Minor thickening of the proximal MCL with no surrounding edema suggestive of previous injury and healing with scarring. On a background of severe mucoid degeneration the body and posterior horn of the lateral meniscus is severely attenuated in keeping with complex degenerate tearing, with a few small parameniscal cysts along the lateral joint line. Ancillary findings described above.

Exam Type: MRI KNEE LEFT WO CONTRAST
Exam Date and Time: [DATE] [TIME]
Indication: 3 weeks of medial left knee pain
Comparison: No relevant prior studies available for comparison.

TECHNIQUE:
MRI of the left knee was performed on a 1.5 Tesla system with a dedicated knee coil in three planes (axial, sagittal, and coronal), using a standard non-contrast protocol.

FINDINGS:
OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:
Alignment is anatomic. No acute fracture or bone bruise. Background marrow signal is normal without infiltrative marrow process. No aggressive osseous lesions.

JOINT SPACE:
No joint effusion. No intra-articular bodies. No Baker's cyst.

MEDIAL COMPARTMENT:
Medial meniscus: Small vertical tear of the posterior horn at the meniscocapsular junction.
Medial compartment cartilage: No focal cartilage defects.

LATERAL COMPARTMENT:
Lateral meniscus: Normal in morphology and signal.
Lateral compartment cartilage: No focal cartilage defects.

PATELLOFEMORAL COMPARTMENT:
Patellofemoral compartment cartilage: No focal cartilage defects.

CRUCIATE LIGAMENTS:
Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL): Normal with both bundles intact.
Posterior cruciate ligament (PCL): Normal.

COLLATERAL LIGAMENTS & POSTEROLATERAL CORNER:
Medial collateral ligament (MCL): Normal.
Lateral collateral ligament (LCL) complex: Normal.
Posterolateral corner structures: Normal.

EXTENSOR MECHANISM:
Distal quadriceps tendon: No tendinosis or tear.
Patella tendon: No tendinosis or tear.
Medial patellofemoral ligament (MPFL) and patellar retinacula: Normal.
Patellofemoral tracking: No edema in superolateral Hoffa's fat pad. No lateral patellar tilt or translation. No patella alta. Normal patellar and trochlear morphology. Normal tibial tubercle-trochlear groove (TT-TG) distance measuring 13 mm.

MUSCLES/TENDONS:
No acute muscle strain or muscle atrophy. Visualized tendons not previously discussed are intact without tendinosis or tear.

SOFT TISSUES:
No soft tissue mass. Normal popliteal neurovascular bundle.

IMPRESSION:
Small vertical tear of the posterior horn of the medial meniscus at the meniscocapsular junction.

Findings:  No significant knee effusion. Normal medial and lateral menisci. No evidence of tears.  Normal ACL, PCL, MCL and LCL. Normal extensor mechanism.  The tibiofemoral articular cartilage is preserved. Moderate - severe thinning of the lateral patellofemoral articular cartilage is noted with mild lateral patellar facet. Underlying bony change.  
Conclusion: Lateral patellofemoral degenerate change. No meniscal injury.
